CYCLICALS LEADCyclicals +3.4% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation has split into a pure barbell, and the defensive side is losing badly. Tech and energy lead the sector table with XLK up 7.14% in a month and XLE up 0.87%, while utilities and real estate sit in the bottom with XLU down 9.12% and XLRE down 8.18%. The spread between XLK and XLU over the year is 48.03% and it sits in the top of its 1-year range. This is capital abandoning yield and safety for growth and commodity exposure, not a broad cyclical recovery.

The theme table confirms this is narrow, not broad. Cyber leads at +29.2% in a month and AI infra at +11.2%, while gold miners and uranium collapse at -13.5% and -19.9%. The average Mag 7 name is up only 7.7% and the average semis name is up 6.5%, both far behind the thematic leaders. The real stress is in small caps: the IWM/QQQ ratio sits in the bottom of its 1-year range with a z-score of -2.36 and a year-to-date decline of 6.33%. You are not in a broadening market. You are in a concentrated tech and commodity trade funded by selling defensives and small caps.

The stretched ratios tell you the pain trade is far from over. XLRE/SPY has a z-score of -3.01 and sits at the absolute bottom of its 1-year range, while XLU/SPY sits at -2.64 and also in the bottom. These are the most oversold sectors relative to the broad market. But the confirmed trend ratios are the ones that matter: SHY/TLT at 2.66, HYG/IEF at 2.59, and QQQ/TLT at 2.16 all sit in the top of their ranges. Credit spreads are tight, short duration is winning, and tech is crushing bonds. Do not fade this rotation until you see credit spreads widen or the XLK/XLU ratio break below its current uptrend.

Growth and commodity leadership versus collapsing defensives and small caps

BULL

XLK leads at 7.14% and cyber at 29.2%, with credit spreads tight and QQQ/TLT at a 1-year high. The risk-on bid is real and confirmed by the HYG/IEF ratio at a z-score of 2.59.

BEAR

IWM/QQQ sits in the bottom of its yearly range with a z-score of -2.36, and XLRE/SPY is at a z-score of -3.01. Breadth is shrinking and the rotation is into a handful of themes, leaving most stocks behind.

TELL

Watch the XLK/XLU ratio. If it holds above its current uptrend at a z-score of 2.69, the narrow tech leadership continues. If it breaks, the defensive rotation has begun.

⚠ Cyclical sectors lead on sector performance with XLK up **7.14%** and XLE up **0.87%**, while XLU and XLRE are down at least **8%**. vs The XLRE/SPY ratio at a z-score of **-3.01** and XLU/SPY at **-2.64** are at the bottom of their yearly ranges, which historically precedes mean reversion in defensives.: The sector performance shows active selling of defensives, but the z-scores show the selling is extreme. Trust the trend while credit ratios like HYG/IEF at **2.59** remain at the top of their ranges, because credit leads equity rotation.
⚠ Credit ratios confirm risk-on with HYG/IEF at a z-score of **2.59** and JNK/TLT at **2.25**, both at 1-year highs. vs Breadth ratios show risk-off with IWM/QQQ at **-2.36** and SIZE/SPY at **-2.45**, both at the bottom of their yearly ranges.: Credit says the risk appetite is strong, but breadth says it is only strong in large caps. Trust the breadth reading for stock selection, because narrow leadership eventually breaks without broad participation.

The most extreme mean-reversion candidates are XLRE/SPY at a z-score of -3.01 and XLU/SPY at -2.64, both in the bottom of their 1-year ranges. Utilities and real estate are this oversold relative to the broad market, and XLRE is down 8.15% year to date against the broad market.

But the confirmed trend extremes are the ones you trade with: SHY/TLT at 2.66, HYG/IEF at 2.59, BKLN/HYG at 2.47, and XLE/XLU at 2.41 all sit in the top of their 1-year ranges with year-to-date ratios up 7.24%, 3.43%, 1.10%, and 50.44% respectively. Credit is calm, short duration is winning, and energy is crushing utilities.

The SIZE/SPY ratio at a z-score of -2.45 and the IWM/QQQ ratio at -2.36 confirm small caps are in a confirmed downtrend, not a reversion setup. Do not buy the defensive dip until those credit ratios roll over.
